claim: Complex I (CI) is the main entry point for electrons into the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mETC).
source: Complex I (CI) is the main entry point for electrons into the mETC.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about CI's role in the mETC.

claim: The cryoEM structure of CI* from Vigna radiata was determined at 3.9 Å resolution.
source: Here, we present the cryoEM structure of the known CI assembly intermediate CI* from Vigna radiata at 3.9 Å resolution.
evidence: The resolution is explicitly stated in the abstract and supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CI* contains CI's NADH-binding and CoQ-binding modules, the proximal-pumping module and the plant-specific γ-carbonic-anhydrase domain (γCA).
source: CI* contains CI's NADH-binding and CoQ-binding modules, the proximal-pumping module and the plant-specific γ-carbonic-anhydrase domain (γCA).
evidence: This composition is directly stated in the abstract and confirmed by the structural analysis presented in the results.

claim: Plant respiratory processes are closely intertwined with photosynthetic pathways.
source: Plant respiratory processes are also closely intertwined with photosynthetic pathways.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the introduction without specific experimental support in this manuscript.

claim: Plant mitochondria possess a 'canonical' mETC composed of four large membrane protein complexes (complexes I-IV, CI-IV) and an associated ATP synthase in the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM).
source: Plant mitochondria possess a 'canonical' mETC shared with most eukaryotes that is composed of four large membrane protein complexes (complexes I-IV, CI-IV) and an associated ATP synthase in the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about plant mitochondrial structure.

claim: Plants possess an 'alternative' mETC that dissipates reduction equivalents in a non-H+-pumping, non-energy-conserving fashion.
source: Additionally, plants also possess an 'alternative' mETC that dissipates reduction equivalents in a non-H+-pumping, non-energy-conserving fashion (Millar et al., 2011; Schertl and Braun, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Complex I is the largest (~1 MDa) component of the mETC in plants.
source: In plants, as in most eukaryotes so far studied, CI is the largest (~1 MDa) and mechanistically least understood component of the mETC (Sazanov, 2015; Hirst, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to previous literature.

claim: CI oxidizes NADH and reduces coenzyme Q (CoQ, ubiquinone), pumping four H+ per two electrons from NADH.
source: CI oxidizes NADH and reduces coenzyme Q (CoQ, ubiquinone), pumping four H+ per two electrons from NADH (Jones et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature establishing this stoichiometry.

claim: CI is an L-shaped multiprotein complex, with a membrane arm and a peripheral arm.
source: CI is an L-shaped multiprotein complex, with a membrane arm and a peripheral arm.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about CI structure.

claim: The peripheral arm of CI extends into the mitochondrial matrix in eukaryotes.
source: In eukaryotes, the peripheral arm of CI extends into the mitochondrial matrix, while the membrane arm is buried within the IMM.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about eukaryotic CI structure.

claim: The peripheral arm contains the NADH dehydrogenase N-module and the CoQ-reducing Q-module.
source: The peripheral arm contains the NADH dehydrogenase N-module and the CoQ-reducing Q-module, which provide the binding sites for NADH and quinone, respectively, as well as the chain of FeS clusters needed for electron transfer (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The membrane arm contains four proton pumps, two in the proximal-pumping module (PP) and two in the distal-pumping module (PD).
source: The membrane arm contains four proton pumps, two of which are located in the proximal-pumping module (PP), with the remaining two pumps in the distal-pumping module (PD; Figure 1A; Dröse et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Five gamma-type carbonic anhydrase (γCA) proteins (CA1, CA2, CA3, CAL1, and CAL2) have been shown to be associated with CI in plants.
source: Most notably, five gamma-type carbonic anhydrase (γCA) proteins (CA1, CA2, CA3, CAL1, and CAL2) have been shown to be associated with CI in plants (Sunderhaus et al., 2006; Perales et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: The γCA proteins are located on the matrix side of CI's membrane arm, likely as a heterotrimer of CAL1 or CAL2 monomer plus a CA1/CA2 hetero- or homodimer.
source: These proteins are located on the matrix side of CI's membrane arm, likely as a heterotrimer of CAL1 or CAL2 monomer plus a CA1/CA2 hetero- or homodimer (Fromm et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: In metazoans, the N-module is assembled onto the rest of the complex (Q-, PP- and PD-modules) as the final step of assembly.
source: In metazoans, the N-module (which is responsible for NADH oxidation) is assembled onto the rest of the complex (Q-, PP- and PD-modules) as the final step of assembly (Formosa et al., 2018; Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2017; Garcia et al., 2017; Stroud et al., 2016; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In plants, the final assembly step is the attachment of the PD-module onto an intermediate (termed CI*) that already contains the N-, Q- and PP-modules.
source: In plants, more similar to what occurs in bacterial CI assembly (Friedrich et al., 2016), the final assembly step is the attachment of the PD-module onto an intermediate (termed CI*) that already contains the N-, Q- and PP-modules (Ligas et al., 2019; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated with citations and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The plant CI* intermediate contains all the subunits and co-factors needed to carry out NADH:CoQ oxidoreduction.
source: In contrast, the plant CI* intermediate contains all the subunits and co-factors needed to carry out NADH:CoQ oxidoreduction.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the structural composition of CI*.

claim: A typical reported yield of mitochondria is ~0.2–0.5 mg mitochondria/g fresh weight of starting plant material.
source: A typical reported yield of mitochondria is ~0.2–0.5 mg mitochondria/g fresh weight of starting plant material (Luster and Fites, 1987), which contrasts with a yield of ~30 mg mitochondria/g fresh weight from mammalian sources.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: Mammalian sources yield ~30 mg mitochondria/g fresh weight.
source: A typical reported yield of mitochondria is ~0.2–0.5 mg mitochondria/g fresh weight of starting plant material (Luster and Fites, 1987), which contrasts with a yield of ~30 mg mitochondria/g fresh weight from mammalian sources.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to plant mitochondrial yields.

claim: V. radiata offers several advantages for plant mitochondrial research including easy sprouting and harvesting within six days.
source: V. radiata offers several advantages for plant mitochondrial research: i) it can be easily sprouted and harvested within six days, ii) it can be grown in the dark (etiolated) to minimize development of chloroplasts, which would otherwise contaminate the mitochondrial preparations, iii) its age and growth conditions can be controlled experimentally, iv) its genome has been sequenced and v) its mitochondrial content has been reported to be higher than other plant sources previously used for plant mitochondrial research (Luster and Fites, 1987).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for choosing V. radiata as the model system.

claim: V. radiata can be grown in the dark (etiolated) to minimize development of chloroplasts.
source: V. radiata offers several advantages for plant mitochondrial research: i) it can be easily sprouted and harvested within six days, ii) it can be grown in the dark (etiolated) to minimize development of chloroplasts, which would otherwise contaminate the mitochondrial preparations, iii) its age and growth conditions can be controlled experimentally, iv) its genome has been sequenced and v) its mitochondrial content has been reported to be higher than other plant sources previously used for plant mitochondrial research (Luster and Fites, 1987).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for choosing V. radiata as the model system.

claim: The mitochondrial content of V. radiata has been reported to be higher than other plant sources previously used for plant mitochondrial research.
source: V. radiata offers several advantages for plant mitochondrial research: i) it can be easily sprouted and harvested within six days, ii) it can be grown in the dark (etiolated) to minimize development of chloroplasts, which would otherwise contaminate the mitochondrial preparations, iii) its age and growth conditions can be controlled experimentally, iv) its genome has been sequenced and v) its mitochondrial content has been reported to be higher than other plant sources previously used for plant mitochondrial research (Luster and Fites, 1987).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: The optimized protocol routinely obtains ~1 g of wet weight mitochondria per 1 kg of etiolated V. radiata hypocotyls.
source: Moreover, we have optimized standard plant mitochondria isolation protocols (Millar et al., 2007) to routinely obtain ~1 g of wet weight mitochondria per 1 kg of etiolated V. radiata hypocotyls, approximately 3–4 times what has been previously reported (Luster and Fites, 1987).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the optimized protocol with a citation to the previous yield.

claim: The optimized mitochondrial yield from V. radiata is approximately 3–4 times what has been previously reported.
source: Moreover, we have optimized standard plant mitochondria isolation protocols (Millar et al., 2007) to routinely obtain ~1 g of wet weight mitochondria per 1 kg of etiolated V. radiata hypocotyls, approximately 3–4 times what has been previously reported (Luster and Fites, 1987).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to previous yields with a citation.

claim: All the cofactors necessary for the transfer of electrons between NADH and CoQ are present in the CI* intermediate.
source: All the cofactors necessary for the transfer of electrons between NADH and CoQ are present in the CI* intermediate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the structural data showing the presence of FMN and FeS clusters.

claim: CI* contains the flavin mononucleotide (FMN) in NDUV1.
source: This includes the flavin mononucleotide (FMN) in NDUV1, all seven FeS-clusters of the main electron transport pathway (N3[V1], N1b[S1], N4[S1], N5[S1], N6a[S8], N6b[S8], N2[S7]), and the off-pathway FeS cluster N1a[V2] (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: CI* contains all seven FeS-clusters of the main electron transport pathway (N3[V1], N1b[S1], N4[S1], N5[S1], N6a[S8], N6b[S8], N2[S7]).
source: This includes the flavin mononucleotide (FMN) in NDUV1, all seven FeS-clusters of the main electron transport pathway (N3[V1], N1b[S1], N4[S1], N5[S1], N6a[S8], N6b[S8], N2[S7]), and the off-pathway FeS cluster N1a[V2] (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: CI* contains the off-pathway FeS cluster N1a[V2].
source: This includes the flavin mononucleotide (FMN) in NDUV1, all seven FeS-clusters of the main electron transport pathway (N3[V1], N1b[S1], N4[S1], N5[S1], N6a[S8], N6b[S8], N2[S7]), and the off-pathway FeS cluster N1a[V2] (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Density can be seen in the cryoEM map in the region of the Q-tunnel, in an equivalent position to that of CoQ in the Y. lipolytica structure.
source: Moreover, density can be seen in the cryoEM map in the region of the Q-tunnel, in an equivalent position to that of CoQ in the Y. lipolytica structure (Parey et al., 2019; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The N-terminus of core Q-module subunit NDUS2 is shortened in V. radiata compared to NDUS2 from Y. lipolytica and mammals.
source: The N-terminus of core Q-module subunit NDUS2 is shortened in V. radiata compared to NDUS2 from Y. lipolytica and mammals, in which the N-terminus of NDUS2 extends from the interface of the peripheral and membrane arms of the complex along the matrix side of the membrane arm.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation comparing V. radiata to other organisms.

claim: V. radiata NDUS2 is ~40 amino acid residues shorter on the N-terminus compared to mammals.
source: In contrast, V. radiata NDUS2 is ~40 amino acid residues shorter on the N-terminus compared to mammals and does not extend along the membrane arm.
evidence: This is stated as a specific structural difference.

claim: The N-terminus of core peripheral arm subunit NDUS8 possesses an additional α-helix in V. radiata that binds between the Q-module accessory subunit NDUA5 and the PP-module core membrane subunit NU2M.
source: In V. radiata, the N-terminus possesses an additional α-helix that binds between the Q-module accessory subunit NDUA5 and the PP-module core membrane subunit NU2M, enlarging the interaction interface between the peripheral and membrane arms (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Core subunit NU2M in V. radiata CI* contains three N-terminal transmembrane helices that are present in yeast and bacterial complexes, but lost in the metazoan lineage.
source: Core subunit NU2M in V. radiata CI* contains three N-terminal transmembrane helices that are present in yeast and bacterial complexes, but lost in the metazoan lineage (Birrell and Hirst, 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: V. radiata CI* contains a homologue of Y. lipolytica's accessory subunit NUXM (absent in metazoans), which binds to the NU2M N-terminal transmembrane helices.
source: Moreover, V. radiata CI* contains a homologue of Y. lipolytica's accessory subunit NUXM (absent in metazoans), which binds to the NU2M N-terminal transmembrane helices.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: The presence of NDUX1 in both plants and fungi suggests that this subunit was present in the ancestral eukaryotic CI before the unikont/bikont lineage divergence but was lost in metazoans.
source: The presence of this subunit in both plants and fungi suggests that this subunit was present in the ancestral eukaryotic CI before the unikont/bikont lineage divergence but was lost in metazoans when NU2M became N-terminally truncated.
evidence: This is stated as an evolutionary inference based on the presence/absence pattern of the subunit.

claim: In the plant complex, the peripheral arm accessory subunit NDUS6 lacks an N-terminal domain that is seen in both the Y. lipolytica and mammalian structures.
source: In the plant complex, the peripheral arm accessory subunit NDUS6 lacks an N-terminal domain that is seen in both the Y. lipolytica and mammalian structures (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The double-CHCH domain of the PP-module NDUA8 subunit is C-terminally truncated in V. radiata compared to both Y. lipolytica and mammals.
source: Compared to both Y. lipolytica and mammals, the double-CHCH domain of the PP-module NDUA8 subunit, which binds to the 'heel' of the complex on the intermembrane space (Figure 2B), is C-terminally truncated in V. radiata.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The PP-module accessory subunit NDUC2 is C-terminally truncated in V. radiata and Y. lipolytica relative to NDUC2 in mammals.
source: The PP-module accessory subunit NDUC2 is also C-terminally truncated in V. radiata and Y. lipolytica relative to NDUC2 in mammals (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Two accessory subunits are absent from the Q-module in the CI* structure, namely the LYR-protein subunit NDUA6 and its accompanying acyl-carrier protein (ACPM1).
source: Compared to the mammalian and Y. lipolytica structures, two accessory subunits are absent from the Q-module in the CI* structure, namely the LYR-protein subunit NDUA6 and its accompanying acyl-carrier protein (ACPM1).
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation comparing CI* to other structures.

claim: When the Y. lipolytica NDUA6 homologue is knocked out or mutated, this severely impacts the activity of the complex.
source: The absence of the NDUA6 and ACPM1 subunits in CI* is notable given that, when the Y. lipolytica NDUA6 homologue is knocked out or mutated, this severely impacts the activity of the complex (Angerer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: V. radiata CI* does not have any plant-specific accessory subunits on the peripheral arm.
source: V. radiata CI* does not have any plant-specific accessory subunits on the peripheral arm.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: A large (~90 kDa) hetero-trimeric γCA domain lies on top of the core membrane arm subunit NU2M.
source: Most notably, a large (~90 kDa) hetero-trimeric γCA domain lies on top of the core membrane arm subunit NU2M (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The three different subunits of V. radiata CI* γCA domain were definitively assigned as CA1, CA2 and CA2L.
source: Based on unambiguous density for key non-conserved residues, we were able to definitively assign the three different subunits of V. radiata CI* as CA1, CA2 and CA2L (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The interaction surface between the γCA domain and the PP-module covers an approximate surface of 3,740 Å2.
source: The interaction surface between the γCA domain and the PP-module (subunits NU2M, NDUC2, P2 and NDUX1) is large, covering an approximate surface of 3,740 Å2.
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative measurement from the structure.

claim: The approximate gain of solvation free energy between the γCA domain and the PP-module is −210 kcal/mol.
source: As expected (Sunderhaus et al., 2006), the γCA interacts with the PP-module tightly, with an approximate gain of solvation free energy of −210 kcal/mol, which is almost twice as large as the solvation energy gain of association of the γCA hetero-trimer itself (Figure 3A, Table 5).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative measurement from the structure with reference to a table.

claim: The N-terminal mitochondrial signal pre-sequences for CA1 and CA2 remain uncleaved.
source: As has been previously demonstrated by proteomic analysis, the N-terminal mitochondrial signal pre-sequences for CA1 and CA2 remain uncleaved (Klodmann et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: The N-terminal sequences of CA1 and CA2 together form a short α-helical coiled-coil-like structure.
source: We show here that these two N-terminal sequences together form a short α-helical coiled-coil-like structure (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The coiled coil formed by CA1 and CA2 N-termini is amphipathic and binds on the matrix surface of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
source: This coiled coil is amphipathic and binds on the matrix surface of the inner mitochondrial membrane, contacting the NDUC2 and P2 subunits (see below) adjacent to the NU2M core subunit.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: No density was observed for the N-terminal pre-sequence of CA2L, consistent with it being post-translationally cleaved.
source: In contrast, no density was observed for the N-terminal pre-sequence of CA2L, consistent with it being post-translationally cleaved (Huang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation with a citation to previous literature.

claim: Recombinant mitochondrial γCA from plants has been shown to bind bicarbonate (HCO3-).
source: Although recombinant mitochondrial γCA from plants has been shown to bind bicarbonate (HCO3-), it remains unclear whether it exhibits enzymatic activity (Martin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: The canonical γCA trimer possesses three active sites, one at each interface between two protomers.
source: The canonical γCA trimer possesses three active sites, one at each interface between two protomers.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about γCA structure.

claim: Each active site in canonical γCA is formed by three essential Zn2+-coordinating histidine residues.
source: Each active site is formed by three essential Zn2+-coordinating histidine residues.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about γCA catalytic sites.

claim: In the plant CI γCA heterotrimer, the CA2L subunit is lacking two of the three essential histidine residues (Ala-147 and Arg-152 in V. radiata) necessary to form active sites at the interfaces with the CA1 and CA2 subunits.
source: However, in the plant CI γCA heterotrimer, the CA2L subunit is lacking two of the three essential histidine residues (Ala-147 and Arg-152 in V. radiata) that would be necessary to form active sites at the interfaces with the CA1 and CA2 subunits.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation from the model.

claim: The V. radiata CA1 subunit is missing one of the three Zn2+-coordinating histidine residues (Gln-135).
source: Furthermore, the V. radiata CA1 subunit is also missing one of the three Zn2+-coordinating histidine residues (Gln-135).
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation from the model.

claim: Only one potentially catalytically active interface with all three Zn2+ coordinating residues remains in V. radiata's γCA—namely, the site between CA1 and CA2.
source: Therefore, only one potentially catalytically active interface with all three Zn2+ coordinating residues remains in V. radiata's γCA—namely, the site between CA1 and CA2 at the "top" (most matrix-exposed periphery) of the domain.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the structural observations.

claim: Clear density for a Zn2+ can only be seen at the CA1-CA2 interface site.
source: Clear density for a Zn2+ can only be seen at this site (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The plant CA1, CA2 and CAL2 proteins belong to the CamH subclass of γCAs, which lack the acidic loop containing the catalytically important 'proton shuttle' glutamate residue.
source: It is also important to note that the plant CA1, CA2 and CAL2 proteins belong to the CamH subclass of γCAs, which lack the acidic loop containing the catalytically important 'proton shuttle' glutamate residue (Glu89 in the canonical γCA from Methanosarcina thermophila) (Zimmerman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: Some members of the CamH subclass are catalytically active, while some are not.
source: While some members of the CamH subclass are catalytically active, some are not (Soto et al., 2006; Jeyakanthan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: The other plant-specific subunit assigned in CI* was the single-transmembrane subunit P2.
source: The other plant-specific subunit we were able to assign in CI* was the single-transmembrane subunit P2.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: P2 binds on top of NDUX1, adjacent to NU2M and directly underneath the γCA domain.
source: This subunit binds on top of NDUX1, adjacent to NU2M and directly underneath the γCA domain.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: P2, NDUX1, NU2M and NDUC2 form a lipid-filled cavity positioned directly below the γCA domain.
source: Together, P2, NDUX1, NU2M and NDUC2 form a lipid-filled cavity positioned directly below the γCA domain (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 3C and D.

claim: The loops that cap the Q-tunnel at the interface of the peripheral and membrane arms of the complex, namely the NU3M TMH1-2 and NU1M TMH5-6 loops, are disordered.
source: The loops that cap the Q-tunnel at the interface of the peripheral and membrane arms of the complex, namely the NU3M TMH1-2 and NU1M TMH5-6 loops, are disordered.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: The disordered state of the Q-tunnel capping loops is analogous to what is observed in the open or deactive structures of the mammalian and Y. lipolytica complexes.
source: This is analogous to what is observed in the open or deactive structures of the mammalian and Y. lipolytica complexes (Agip et al., 2018; Letts et al., 2019; Parey et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: A π-bulge in NU6M's TMH3 in mammals has been seen to undergo a major conformational change, refolding into an α-helix during complex I's open-to-closed transition.
source: In particular, a π-bulge in NU6M's TMH3 in mammals has been seen to undergo a major conformational change, refolding into an α-helix during complex I's open-to-closed transition (Agip et al., 2018; Letts et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: The π-bulge in NU6M's TMH3 is also present in V. radiata CI*.
source: This π-bulge in NU6M's TMH3 is also present in V. radiata CI*.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: The 'E-channel' and the hydrophilic axis of polar amino acid residues that are involved in proton translocation and span the membrane arm of CI are evident in V. radiata CI*.
source: The 'E-channel' (Baradaran et al., 2013) and the hydrophilic axis of polar amino acid residues that are involved in proton translocation and span the membrane arm of CI are also evident in V. radiata CI* (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Hydrophilic-axis residue Lys399 on NU2M's TMH12 is exposed to the midplane of the membrane in CI*.
source: Given the lack of additional accessory subunits or assembly factors to cap the end of CI*'s shortened membrane arm, hydrophilic-axis residue Lys399 on NU2M's TMH12 is exposed to the midplane of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation and inference.

claim: The lack of NDUS6 N-terminal domain may in part explain observed differences between the assembly pathways of plant and opisthokont CI.
source: Thus, the lack of the NDUS6 N-terminus may in part explain observed differences between the assembly pathways of plant and opisthokont CI (see Discussion).
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural differences observed.

claim: The pattern of truncated core and accessory subunits or missing interactions in V. radiata relative to those in opisthokonts likely diminishes the stability of the attachment of PP-module to the PD-module.
source: This pattern of truncated core and accessory subunits or missing interactions (e.g. NDUS2, NDUA8 and NDUC2; Table 4) in V. radiata relative to those in opisthokonts likely diminishes the stability of the attachment of PP-module to the PD-module, which may have consequences for CI's function and assembly (see Discussion).
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural observations.

claim: CI* is an established assembly intermediate of plant CI, previously identified with genetic and proteomic studies in non-etiolated seedlings and mature leaves of A. thaliana and N. sylvestris.
source: CI* is an established assembly intermediate of plant CI, previously identified with genetic and proteomic studies in non-etiolated seedlings and mature leaves of A. thaliana and N. sylvestris (Ligas et al., 2019; Meyer et al., 2011; Schertl et al., 2012; Schimmeyer et al., 2016; Senkler et al., 2017; Pineau et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: CI* exhibits NADH-dehydrogenase activity in in-gel activity assays.
source: Furthermore, CI* exhibits NADH-dehydrogenase activity in in-gel activity assays (Meyer et al., 2011; Pineau et al., 2008; Haïli et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: The V. radiata CI* showed NADH-DQ oxidoreductase activity using a standard CI spectroscopic activity assay.
source: Moreover, these fractions also showed NADH-decylubiquinone oxidoreductase activity using a standard CI spectroscopic activity assay (Huang et al., 2015; Figure 1—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F.

claim: A mutant of Y. lipolytica CI in which the PD-module accessory subunit NB8M is deleted (nb8mΔ) fails to assemble the PD-module.
source: A mutant of Y. lipolytica CI in which the PD-module accessory subunit NB8M (homologue of plant NDUB7) is deleted (nb8mΔ) fails to assemble the PD-module (Dröse et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: The nb8mΔ mutant CI is a functional H+-pumping NADH-CoQ oxidoreductase with a reduced H+:e- ratio of 2H+:2e-.
source: The nb8mΔ mutant CI is a functional H+-pumping NADH-CoQ oxidoreductase. However, its H+:e- ratio, which is normally 4H+:2e- in fully assembled CI, is reduced to 2H+:2e- (Dröse et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: Deletion of E. coli NuoL or truncation of its transmembrane helices 15–16 result in a functional CI mutant whose H+:e- coupling is 2H+:2e-.
source: Deletion of NuoL or truncation of its transmembrane helices 15–16, which bridge the PP and PD modules, result in a functional CI mutant whose H+:e- coupling is 2H+:2e- (Steimle et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: A lower-H+-pumping CI* could provide additional flexibility to plants' bioenergetic regulation, beyond the interplay between the canonical and alternative pathways of the mETC.
source: We hypothesize that a lower-H+-pumping CI* could provide additional flexibility to plants' bioenergetic regulation, beyond the interplay between the canonical and alternative pathways of the mETC.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the structural and functional observations.

claim: Having a 2H+:2e- ratio would allow CI* to contribute to ATP generation in situations where the mitochondrial [NAD+]/[NADH] ratio would not support H+ pumping by CI.
source: For instance, having a 2H+:2e- ratio would allow CI* to contribute to ATP generation in situations where the mitochondrial [NAD+]/[NADH] ratio would not support H+ pumping by CI (see Appendix for an in-depth discussion).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the proposed 2H+:2e- stoichiometry.

claim: The structure of V. radiata CI* is the first atomic resolution structure of any plant mitochondrial electron transport chain complex.
source: The structure of V. radiata CI* presented here is the first atomic resolution structure of any plant mitochondrial electron transport chain complex and reveals several key features of mitochondrial CI from vascular plants.
evidence: This is stated as a claim about the novelty of the work.

claim: CI* is composed of over 30 subunits of the N-module, Q-module, PP-module and the γCA domain.
source: As expected from complexome profiling analyses (Ligas et al., 2019; Senkler et al., 2017), our structure of CI* is composed of over 30 subunits of the N-module, Q-module, PP-module and the γCA domain.
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature and supported by the structural data.

claim: CI* is missing the two membrane arm core subunits NU4M and NU5M and their associated accessory subunits that form the PD-module.
source: However, it is missing the two membrane arm core subunits NU4M and NU5M and their associated accessory subunits that form the PD-module (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In opisthokonts, the interaction between NDUS6, NDUA12 and the NDUA12-homologous assembly factor NDUFAF2 establishes an important checkpoint for assembly of the peripheral arm.
source: In opisthokonts, the interaction between NDUS6, NDUA12 and the NDUA12-homologous assembly factor NDUFAF2 establishes an important checkpoint for assembly of the peripheral arm.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about opisthokont CI assembly.

claim: In plants, NDUS6 may assemble on CI independent of the status of NDUFAF2/NDUA12.
source: Thus, in plants, NDUS6 may assemble on CI independent of the status of NDUFAF2/NDUA12.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural differences in NDUS6.

claim: Attaching the N-module before the PD-module in plants may provide additional flexibility to their mitochondrial ETC.
source: Furthermore, attaching the N-module before the PD-module in plants may provide additional flexibility to their mitochondrial ETC (see discussion below and Appendix).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the assembly pathway differences.

claim: The interface between the PP- and PD-modules is more extensively stabilized by accessory subunit interactions in mammals than in Y. lipolytica or V. radiata.
source: It is clear from the currently available structures that the interface between the PP-module and PD-module is more extensively stabilized by accessory subunit interactions in mammals than in Y. lipolytica or V. radiata (Table 4).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on structural comparisons with reference to a table.

claim: The lack of the NDUA8 and NDUC2 bridging interactions suggest that the interface between the PP- and PD-modules in plants may be weaker.
source: The lack of the NDUA8 and NDUC2 bridging interactions suggest that the interface between the PP- and PD-modules in plants may be weaker, which may also help explain the differences in the CI assembly pathway in plants versus opisthokonts.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural observations.

claim: Only three assembly factors have been identified in plants: L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase (GLDH), the FeS protein INDH and an LYR protein termed CIAF1.
source: In plants, only three assembly factors have been thus far identified: L-galactono-1,4-lactone dehydrogenase (GLDH) (Senkler et al., 2017), the FeS protein INDH (Wydro et al., 2013) and an LYR protein termed CIAF1 (Ivanova et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: Current models of plant CI biogenesis predict that only GLDH should be bound to the CI* intermediate.
source: Current models of plant CI biogenesis predict that, of these three, only GLDH should be bound to the CI* intermediate (Ligas et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: GLDH is a large (~60 kDa) globular enzyme.
source: However, GLDH is a large (~60 kDa) globular enzyme (Leferink et al., 2008), for which we do not see any consistent density in our structure.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: The structure allowed the authors to define the interface between the γCA domain and the membrane arm of CI.
source: The structure also allowed us to define the interface between the γCA domain and the membrane arm of CI and revealed a key role for lipids in this interaction.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the structural analysis.

claim: Lipids play a key role in the interaction between the γCA domain and the membrane arm.
source: The structure also allowed us to define the interface between the γCA domain and the membrane arm of CI and revealed a key role for lipids in this interaction.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the structural analysis.

claim: There are significant steady-state amounts of CI* in V. radiata mitochondria under etiolating conditions.
source: This suggests that there are significant steady-state amounts of CI*in V. radiata mitochondria under these etiolating conditions and that CI* may be playing an independent physiological function beyond its role in CI assembly.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the ability to isolate sufficient amounts of CI*.

claim: CI* may be playing an independent physiological function beyond its role in CI assembly.
source: This suggests that there are significant steady-state amounts of CI*in V. radiata mitochondria under these etiolating conditions and that CI* may be playing an independent physiological function beyond its role in CI assembly.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the abundance of CI*.

claim: The structure of V. radiata CI* provides information on mitochondrial CI composition, assembly and evolution.
source: The structure of V. radiata CI* presented here provides a wealth of information on mitochondrial CI composition, assembly and evolution and raises several questions on the dynamics and regulation of plant respiration.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the contributions of the work.

claim: The structure raises questions on the dynamics and regulation of plant respiration.
source: The structure of V. radiata CI* presented here provides a wealth of information on mitochondrial CI composition, assembly and evolution and raises several questions on the dynamics and regulation of plant respiration.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the implications of the work.

claim: The most detailed plant CI structures known prior to this work were obtained by negative-stain electron microscopy (EM) two-dimensional (2D) classifications from Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Arabidopsis thaliana or sub-tomogram averaged reconstructions that lack secondary structure details.
source: In contrast to the large number of recent high-resolution structures of mammalian and yeast respiratory complexes and supercomplexes, the most detailed plant CI structures known were obtained by negative-stain electron microscopy (EM) two-dimensional (2D) classifications from Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Arabidopsis thaliana or sub-tomogram averaged reconstructions that lack secondary structure details (Bultema et al., 2009; Dudkina et al., 2005; Davies et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: The paucity of functional and structural data for plant mETC complexes stems in large part from the limited availability of sufficient protein sample needed for structural analysis.
source: The paucity of functional and structural data for plant mETC complexes stems in large part from the limited availability of sufficient protein sample needed for structural analysis (Dudkina et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: It has been difficult to obtain intact plant mitochondria in sufficient amounts for preparative biochemical fractionation.
source: Indeed, it has been difficult to obtain intact plant mitochondria in sufficient amounts for preparative biochemical fractionation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the challenges in plant mitochondrial research.

claim: Most of the biochemical data on plant mETC have used intact mitochondria or complexes that have been electro-eluted from electrophoretic gels.
source: In light of these challenges, most of the biochemical data on plant mETC have used intact mitochondria (e.g. oxygen-consumption experiments) or complexes that have been electro-eluted from electrophoretic gels (Bultema et al., 2009; Dudkina et al., 2005; Dudkina et al., 2006; Eubel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: Electro-eluted protein samples have yielded low-resolution structures and have proven suitable for proteomic studies.
source: Although such electro-eluted protein samples have yielded the low-resolution structures described above and have proven suitable for proteomic studies, the low yields and low activities of these protein samples have so far thwarted detailed functional or structural analyses of the plant mETC complexes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the limitations of previous methods.

claim: The low yields and low activities of electro-eluted protein samples have thwarted detailed functional or structural analyses of the plant mETC complexes.
source: Although such electro-eluted protein samples have yielded the low-resolution structures described above and have proven suitable for proteomic studies, the low yields and low activities of these protein samples have so far thwarted detailed functional or structural analyses of the plant mETC complexes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the limitations of previous methods.

claim: The structure reveals important differences in the CI core and accessory subunits between plants, mammals, yeast and bacteria.
source: Our structure allowed us to build the first atomic model for any mitochondrial CI species from the plant kingdom and revealed important differences in the CI core and accessory subunits between plants, mammals, yeast and bacteria.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the structural analysis.

claim: The subunit differences shed light on the known differences in CI assembly in plants versus opisthokonts.
source: Such subunit differences shed light on the known differences in CI assembly in plants versus opisthokonts.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural observations.

claim: Adding the NADH dehydrogenase N-module last in metazoans ensures that no assembly intermediate is capable of transferring electrons from NADH to CoQ.
source: In metazoans, adding the NADH dehydrogenase N-module last ensures that no assembly intermediate is capable of transferring electrons from NADH to CoQ.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about metazoan CI assembly.

claim: Adding the N-module last in metazoans is believed to have protective roles, to prevent the formation of reactive oxygen species during the CI assembly process.
source: This is believed to have protective roles, to prevent the formation of reactive oxygen species during the CI assembly process (Parey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: In Y. lipolytica, the N-terminus of NDUS2 binds to the matrix surface of core H+-pumping subunit NU2M.
source: Whereas in Y. lipolytica the N-terminus of NDUS2 binds to the matrix surface of core H+-pumping subunit NU2M, in mammals the N-terminus of NDUS2 extends further along the membrane arm and binds to the matrix surface of core H+-pumping subunit NU4M, bridging across the PP- and PD-modules.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In mammals, the N-terminus of NDUS2 extends further along the membrane arm and binds to the matrix surface of core H+-pumping subunit NU4M, bridging across the PP- and PD-modules.
source: Whereas in Y. lipolytica the N-terminus of NDUS2 binds to the matrix surface of core H+-pumping subunit NU2M, in mammals the N-terminus of NDUS2 extends further along the membrane arm and binds to the matrix surface of core H+-pumping subunit NU4M, bridging across the PP- and PD-modules.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: The equivalent path for the Y. lipolytica or mammalian NDUS2 N-terminus in V. radiata is blocked by the γCA domain to the plant PP-module on the membrane arm.
source: Moreover, the equivalent path for the Y. lipolytica or mammalian NDUS2 N-terminus in V. radiata is blocked by the γCA domain to the plant PP-module on the membrane arm.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: In Y. lipolytica, the N-terminus of NDUS8 forms an extended coil that reaches up along the peripheral arm between the Q-module accessory subunits NDUA5 and NDUA7, making contact with the core Q-module subunit NDUS3.
source: In Y. lipolytica, the N-terminus of NDUS8 forms an extended coil that reaches up along the peripheral arm between the Q-module accessory subunits NDUA5 and NDUA7, making contact with the core Q-module subunit NDUS3.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: The N-terminus of mammalian NDUS8 folds back along the surface of the membrane arm and tucks underneath the Q-module accessory subunit NDUA7.
source: In contrast, the N-terminus of mammalian NDUS8 folds back along the surface of the membrane arm and tucks underneath the Q-module accessory subunit NDUA7.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In Y. lipolytica, the binding site underneath NDUA7 is occupied by NUZM's C-terminus, which folds back under itself.
source: In Y. lipolytica, this binding site, underneath the NDUA7 homologue (NUZM), is occupied by NUZM's C-terminus, which folds back under itself.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In V. radiata, the binding site underneath NDUA7 is occupied by an unidentified subunit that extends toward the core transmembrane subunits adjacent to the NU3M transmembrane helix (TMH) 1–2 loop and the NU6M TMH3.
source: However, in V. radiata the binding site underneath NDUA7 is occupied by an unidentified subunit that extends from this pocket under NDUA7 toward the core transmembrane subunits adjacent to the NU3M transmembrane helix (TMH) 1–2 loop and the NU6M TMH3, which undergo conformational changes during CI's enzymatic turnover in the fungal structures (Agip et al., 2018; Letts et al., 2019; Parey et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation with citations to previous literature.

claim: The NU3M TMH1-2 loop and the NU6M TMH3 undergo conformational changes during CI's enzymatic turnover in the fungal structures.
source: However, in V. radiata the binding site underneath NDUA7 is occupied by an unidentified subunit that extends from this pocket under NDUA7 toward the core transmembrane subunits adjacent to the NU3M transmembrane helix (TMH) 1–2 loop and the NU6M TMH3, which undergo conformational changes during CI's enzymatic turnover in the fungal structures (Agip et al., 2018; Letts et al., 2019; Parey et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: The unidentified sequence in the V. radiata structure appears to be unique to plant CI.
source: Although the identity of this sequence in the V. radiata structure remains unclear, it appears to be unique to plant CI.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the absence of this feature in other structures.

claim: The first transmembrane helix of NU2M in Y. lipolytica is notably short (only 15 amino acids) and enters only to the midplane of the membrane.
source: The first transmembrane helix of NU2M in Y. lipolytica is notably short (only 15 amino acids), enters only to the midplane of the membrane and is bound by a membrane-penetrating loop of the accessory subunit NUXM.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In bacteria (T. thermophilus and E. coli) and V. radiata, the first transmembrane helix of NU2M spans the full length of the membrane.
source: In contrast, in bacteria (T. thermophilus and E. coli) and V. radiata, the first transmembrane helix of NU2M spans the full length of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: The loop connecting V. radiata's NU2M TMH1-2 in the mitochondrial matrix is longer than in any of the other CI structures and extends into the matrix, where it contacts the N-terminal helix of NDUS8.
source: Furthermore, the loop connecting V. radiata's NU2M TMH1-2 in the mitochondrial matrix is longer than in any of the other CI structures and extends into the matrix, where it contacts the N-terminal helix of NDUS8 discussed above.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: The additional interaction surface formed by NDUS8 and NU2M in V. radiata CI is likely functionally relevant given the universality of the hinging motion between CI's peripheral and membrane arms.
source: Given the universality of the hinging motion between CI's peripheral and membrane arms, seen in the structures of several organisms (Agip et al., 2018; Letts et al., 2019; Parey et al., 2018), the additional interaction surface formed by NDUS8 and NU2M in V. radiata CI is likely functionally relevant.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural observations and citations to previous literature.

claim: In opisthokonts, the C-terminal, Zn2+-containing domain of NDUS6 binds mainly to the core subunits NDUS1, NDUS8 and NDUS2 at the interface of the N- and Q-modules.
source: In Y. lipolytica, mammals and V. radiata, the C-terminal, Zn2+-containing domain of NDUS6 binds mainly to the core subunits NDUS1, NDUS8 and NDUS2 at the interface of the N- and Q-modules.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In opisthokonts, the N-terminal domain of NDUS6 binds to the Q-module at an additional site through contacts with the membrane-anchored NDUA9 accessory subunit.
source: However, in opisthokonts, the N-terminal domain of NDUS6 binds to the Q-module at an additional site through contacts with the membrane-anchored NDUA9 accessory subunit (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In opisthokonts, NDUS6 extends above the C-terminus of accessory subunit NDUA12 in order to bind across two locations.
source: In order to bind across these two locations, NDUS6 in opisthokonts extends above the C-terminus of accessory subunit NDUA12.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In opisthokonts, NDUA12 must be bound to the peripheral arm before the N-terminal domain of NDUS6 binds.
source: This arrangement determines the order of assembly of these subunits in opisthokonts, as NDUA12 must be bound to the peripheral arm before the N-terminal domain of NDUS6 binds.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural arrangement.

claim: Due to the lack of the N-terminal domain in V. radiata's NDUS6, there is no interaction with NDUA9 nor traversing of the NDUA12 C-terminus.
source: However, due to the lack of the N-terminal domain in V. radiata's NDUS6, there is no interaction with NDUA9 nor traversing of the NDUA12 C-terminus.
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation.

claim: In Y. lipolytica, the C-terminus of NDUA8 folds back onto itself with an additional α-helix, forming a bulkier subunit and a further interaction interface with the core transmembrane subunit NU1M.
source: In the Y. lipolytica structure, the C-terminus of NDUA8 folds back onto itself with an additional α-helix, forming a bulkier subunit and a further interaction interface with the core transmembrane subunit NU1M.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In mammals, the C-terminus of NDUA8 extends as a long coil halfway along the membrane arm and binds in a pocket between NU2M and NU4M at the interface of the PP-module and PD-module.
source: More interestingly, in mammals, the C-terminus of NDUA8 extends as a long coil halfway along the membrane arm and binds in a pocket between NU2M and NU4M at the interface of the PP-module and PD-module.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In all mitochondrial CI structures to date, NDUC2 binds to the final transmembrane helix of the core NU2M subunit.
source: In all mitochondrial CI structures to date, this subunit binds to the final transmembrane helix of the core NU2M subunit.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In mammals, the NDUC2 C-terminus forms an extended coil on the intermembrane space side of the complex that extends along the membrane arm to interact with NDUB10 and NDUB11, bridging the PP- and PD- modules.
source: However, in mammals, the NDUC2 C-terminus forms an extended coil on the intermembrane space side of the complex that extends along the membrane arm to interact with NDUB10 and NDUB11, bridging the PP- and PD- modules.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: In Y. lipolytica, the bridging interaction between PP and PD modules is present via an extended loop on the PD-module core subunit NU4M.
source: This bridging interaction is also present in Y. lipolytica via an extended loop on the PD-module core subunit NU4M.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of structural features across organisms.

claim: Conformational changes in the Q-tunnel capping loops are thought to play an important role in CI's coupling mechanism.
source: Conformational changes in these loops are thought to play an important role in CI's coupling mechanism, which transduces the energy of NADH-quinone oxidoreduction in the Q module to proton pumping along the membrane arm (Parey et al., 2018; Cabrera-Orefice et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: In all other structures of CI, the final transmembrane core subunit NU5M contains a transmembrane helix (TMH15) that caps the hydrophilic axis at the end of the transmembrane arm of full-length CI.
source: In all other structures of CI, the final transmembrane core subunit NU5M contains a transmembrane helix (TMH15) that caps the hydrophilic axis at the end of the transmembrane arm of full-length CI.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to other CI structures.

claim: The lack of a cap on V. radiata NU2M in CI* suggests that the core hydrophilic axis may be in contact with lipid.
source: The lack of such a cap on V. radiata NU2M in CI* suggests that, although Lys399 of NU2M is mostly surrounded by protein, the core hydrophilic axis may be in contact with lipid.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the structural observations.

claim: The membrane-extraction conditions used (1% w:v digitonin, 4:1 g:g detergent:protein) are very gentle and were chosen after optimization to preserve protein:protein interactions in protein complexes and supercomplexes.
source: Firstly, our membrane-extraction conditions (1% w:v digitonin, 4:1 g:g detergent:protein; see Materials and methods) are very gentle and were chosen after optimization to preserve protein:protein interactions in protein complexes and supercomplexes.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail to support the argument that CI* is not a degradation product.

claim: Immediately after extraction, the detergent-extracted complexes are stabilized with amphipathic polymers, which wrap around the complexes and further protect them from degradation/dissociation.
source: Furthermore, immediately after extraction, we stabilize the detergent-extracted complexes with amphipathic polymers, which wrap around the complexes and further protect them from degradation/dissociation (Breibeck and Rompel, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with a citation.

claim: A large section of membrane stabilized and co-purified by the gentle digitonin/amphipol treatment is clearly seen around the perimeter of CI* at low contour.
source: A large section of membrane stabilized and co-purified by our gentle digitonin/amphipol treatment is clearly seen around the perimeter of CI* at low contour (Figure 1—figure supplement 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4E.

claim: An A. thaliana complexome profiling study using 5% digitonin obtained not only full-length CI and CI*, but also full-length CI in a higher order assembly with complex III (supercomplex SC I+III2).
source: Secondly, using digitonin at a higher concentration (5% w:v), an A. thaliana complexome profiling study (Senkler et al., 2017) obtained not only full-length CI and CI*, but also full-length CI in a higher order assembly with complex III (supercomplex SC I+III2) [Bultema et al., 2009; Dudkina et al., 2005; Eubel et al., 2004a; Eubel et al., 2004b].
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: Protein:protein interactions between complexes in supercomplexes are known to be more labile than intra-complex protein:protein interactions.
source: Protein:protein interactions between complexes in supercomplexes are known to be more labile than intra-complex protein:protein interactions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The more fragile CI:CIII2 interactions are maintained in 5% digitonin.
source: Given that the more fragile CI:CIII2 interactions are maintained in 5% digitonin (Senkler et al., 2017), this argues that the presence of CI* —both in Senkler et al., 2017 and in this study— is not due to a digitonin-induced dissociation of the PD domain, but rather that it is the true assembly intermediate.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature as part of an argument.

claim: Controlled-degradation experiments of plant CI in the presence of harsh detergents have shown that plant CI's detergent-induced dissociation occurs via detachment of the full peripheral arm (PP-PD) from the full matrix arm (N-Q).
source: Thirdly, controlled-degradation experiments of plant CI in the presence of harsh detergents have shown that, analogous to mammalian CI, plant CI's detergent-induced dissociation occurs via detachment of the full peripheral arm (PP-PD) from the full matrix arm (N-Q) (Klodmann et al., 2010), not by dissociation between the PP and PD modules.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: The CI* fraction retains its in-gel and spectroscopic NADH-oxidase activity and chromatographic peak for several days, even after freeze/thaw cycles.
source: Fourthly, we have reproducibly obtained the CI* fraction, which retains its in-gel and spectroscopic NADH-oxidase activity and chromatographic peak for several days, even after freeze/thaw cycles.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: The structure corresponds to the CI* assembly intermediate, rather than to a degradation product of V. radiata CI.
source: For these reasons, it is evident that our structure corresponds to the CI* assembly intermediate, rather than to a degradation product of V. radiata CI.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the evidence presented.

claim: The structure unambiguously resolves the identities of the hetero-trimeric components of the γCA domain of etiolated V. radiata as CA1, CA2 and CA2L.
source: Furthermore, our structure unambiguously resolves the identities of the hetero-trimeric components of the γCA domain of etiolated V. radiata as CA1, CA2 and CA2L.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the structural analysis.

claim: Whether the combination of γCA subunits and the active site arrangements are different in different species, tissues or developmental stages remains to be confirmed.
source: Nevertheless, whether the combination of γCA subunits and, consequently, the active site arrangements are different in different species, tissues or developmental stages (Sunderhaus et al., 2006; Perales et al., 2004; Fromm et al., 2016; Cï Rdoba et al., 2019) remains to be confirmed.
evidence: This is stated as an open question with citations to previous literature.

claim: Structure alone is not sufficient to demonstrate catalytic ability of the plant CI γCA domain.
source: Structure alone is not sufficient to demonstrate catalytic ability of the plant CI γCA domain.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the structural approach.

claim: Despite extensive attempts, no catalytic activity of plant mitochondrial γCAs has been measured to date.
source: Indeed, only bicarbonate binding to the plant mitochondrial γCAs has been shown (Martin et al., 2009) and, despite extensive attempts, no catalytic activity has been measured to date (Fromm et al., 2016; Martin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: Further functional and structural studies with purified CI or CI* samples are necessary to determine whether the γCA domain possesses enzymatic activity.
source: Further functional and structural studies with purified CI or CI* samples are necessary to determine whether the γCA domain possesses enzymatic activity.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation for future research.

claim: In opisthokonts, the assembly factor NDUFAF2 –a paralogue of NDUA12 that occupies the same binding site—sterically prevents the binding of NDUS6.
source: Moreover, the assembly factor NDUFAF2 –a paralogue of NDUA12 that occupies the same binding site—sterically prevents the binding of NDUS6 (Parey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: In opisthokonts, NDUFAF2 must be removed and replaced with NDUA12 before NDUS6 can bind on the peripheral arm to complete the assembly of CI.
source: Thus, in opisthokonts, NDUFAF2 must be removed and replaced with NDUA12 before NDUS6 can bind on the peripheral arm to complete the assembly of CI.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about opisthokont CI assembly.

claim: A NDUFAF2 homologue on CI has yet to be observed experimentally in plants.
source: In plants, a NDUFAF2 homologue on CI has yet to be observed experimentally (Meyer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous literature.

claim: Identification of other possible bridging interactions across the PP- and PD-modules in plants will have to await the structure of full-length plant CI.
source: Identification of other possible bridging interactions across the PP- and PD-modules in plants will have to await the structure of full-length plant CI.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the current study and a direction for future research.

claim: The nb8mΔ mutant subcomplex is analogous to CI*, as it lacks only the PD-module.
source: The resulting CI subcomplex is analogous to CI*, as it lacks only the PD-module.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between the yeast mutant and plant CI*.

claim: The reduced H+:e- ratio in the nb8mΔ mutant is consistent with two of the four H+-pumping subunits (NU4M and NU5M) being absent.
source: This is consistent with two of the four H+-pumping subunits (NU4M and NU5M) being absent in the nb8mΔ mutant subcomplex.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the composition of the mutant.

claim: CI* may provide additional energy-converting flexibility to plants' electron flow and energy conservation.
source: Thus, CI* may provide additional energy-converting flexibility to plants' electron flow and energy conservation.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the proposed function of CI*.

claim: The flexibility provided by CI* would be analogous to the flexibility seen for the electron transport chain of chloroplasts.
source: This would be analogous to the flexibility seen for the electron transport chain of chloroplasts, which employ several dynamic mechanisms at different levels of regulation to adjust the H+:e- coupling and the energetic and redox outputs to changing environmental conditions (Heber and Kirk, 1975; Scheibe et al., 2005; Rochaix, 2011; Murchie and Ruban, 2020).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: In order to address questions on the dynamics and regulation of plant respiration, further research is needed into the structures of the fully assembled plant mitochondrial CI, as well as of its supercomplex with CIII2.
source: In order to address these questions, further research is needed into the structures of the fully assembled plant mitochondrial CI, as well as of its supercomplex with CIII2.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation for future research.

claim: Biochemical, cell biological and genetic approaches are paramount to test hypotheses on the potential functions of CI*.
source: In addition, biochemical, cell biological and genetic approaches are paramount to test hypotheses on the potential functions of CI*.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation for future research.
